name: firesmoke
licence: Apache-2.0 (architecture, Megvii YOLOX) / project's own weights (trained in-house)
licence_verified: 2026-09-16. Architecture is YOLOX-Nano (Apache-2.0, Megvii). Weights are a from-scratch fine-tune of the Apache-2.0 COCO-pretrained yolox_nano.pth checkpoint on D-Fire, trained by this project - not a downloaded third-party checkpoint.
source: Fine-tuned in-house. Base checkpoint: https://github.com/Megvii-BaseDetection/YOLOX/releases/tag/0.1.1rc0 (yolox_nano.pth, Apache-2.0). Training data: D-Fire, obtained via a Kaggle mirror https://www.kaggle.com/datasets/sayedgamal99/smoke-fire-detection-yolo (CC0-1.0 as declared by that listing) which repackages the original D-Fire dataset https://github.com/gaiasd/DFireDataset (see PLAN.md section 5.1 and NOTICE.md for the CC0 caveat on D-Fire's own images).

training.recipe: PLAN.md section 5.3, adapted for a single 4GB-VRAM laptop GPU (GTX 1650) rather than the rented-GPU recipe originally specified
training.base_checkpoint: yolox_nano.pth (COCO-pretrained, 80-class head discarded and reinitialised to 2 classes)
training.dataset_split: D-Fire via Kaggle mirror: 14122 train / 3099 val / 4306 test images (converted YOLO->COCO by training/scripts/dfire_to_coco.py)
training.hardware: NVIDIA GeForce GTX 1650 (4GB VRAM), CUDA 12.4, torch 2.6.0+cu124
training.final_losses_epoch_40: total_loss ~3.4-8.0 (mosaic off, L1 loss active), iou_loss ~1.1-3.1 - see training/YOLOX/YOLOX_outputs/fire_nano/train_log.txt for the full curve
training.in_training_eval: DISABLED. yolox.evaluators.coco_evaluator unconditionally imports a JIT-compiled C++ extension (yolox.layers.COCOeval_opt) that needs an MSVC toolchain not present on the training machine; left enabled it crashed the training loop outright (silently, since trainer.py's train() wraps the loop in try/except/finally and logs a misleading 'Training of experiment is done' regardless of success - this happened once during training, see training/watchdog_train.sh and exps/custom/fire_nano.py for the full incident writeup and fix). Not a real loss of signal: PLAN.md section 5.4 explicitly says not to tune this model on COCO mAP - the real evaluation is false-alarms/hour on continuous site video through the full pipeline including the K-of-N temporal gate, which has NOT been done yet for this checkpoint.
training.validation_status: UNVALIDATED beyond training loss convergence. Per PLAN.md section 5.4 and section 9.3, do not treat this checkpoint as deployment-ready until: (1) false-alarm rate is measured on hours of real site footage through the full pipeline (K-of-N gate included), (2) recall is checked on the D-Fire test split (4306 images, held out but not automatically scored since in-training eval was disabled), (3) site negatives per PLAN.md section 5.2 are collected and the model is re-evaluated against them - this checkpoint was trained on D-Fire alone, with no site-specific negatives yet.

preprocessing.resize: letterbox to the model input size, pad value 114, ratio = min(H_in/h, W_in/w), top-left placement
preprocessing.colour_note: Trained and exported through the same Megvii YOLOX pipeline as yolox_person (backend/models/yolox_person/manifest.json) - no colour conversion anywhere in the training or export path, so this model expects BGR input exactly like the official Megvii exports. See yolox_person's manifest for the measured ~25% recall cost of getting this wrong.

files.note: 40-epoch fine-tune from COCO-pretrained yolox_nano.pth on D-Fire (14122/3099/4306 train/val/test), trained on a GTX 1650. In-training COCO eval was disabled (no MSVC toolchain on the training machine) - validate false-alarm rate on real site video per PLAN.md section 5.4 before deployment, not COCO mAP. See 'training' and 'training.validation_status' above.

io.anchor_note: anchors = sum over strides 8/16/32 of (H/s * W/s). 416 -> 52^2+26^2+13^2 = 3549, same as yolox_person's 416 input.
io.class_order_note: Class order is 0=fire, 1=smoke, matching PLAN.md section 5.3 and src/perimeter/detect/firesmoke.py's FIRE_CLASS_ID=0/SMOKE_CLASS_ID=1. IMPORTANT: the D-Fire Kaggle mirror's own data.yaml declares the OPPOSITE YOLO label convention (names: ['smoke','fire'], i.e. its class 0=smoke, class 1=fire). training/scripts/dfire_to_coco.py remaps this correctly during YOLO->COCO conversion (verified against the label files' own class-frequency distribution, which matches D-Fire's published global box counts: fire 14692 > smoke 11865) - this model's output order does NOT need any further remapping at inference time.
